hook: Capstone two: an agent that ingests CSVs, answers in **DuckDB SQL**, draws charts, and CANNOT write to your database — GA-19's theory as a working build.

scenes.title: CSV → Parquet → views: **ingest once, query everything**
scenes.sub: The GA-19 pipeline, built for real
scenes.narration: The agent's foundation is GA-19's DuckDB pattern, production-hardened. INGESTION: uploaded CSVs — or a watched folder — normalize into Parquet: types inferred and CONFIRMED — 'order_date parsed as date, 3 rows rejected: unparsable'; a rejected-rows file accompanies every ingest, so 'we dropped bad data' is never silent; and DuckDB VIEWS over the Parquet give the model a stable table namespace — 'orders', 'customers' — decoupled from files. Schema grounding: DESCRIBE plus sampled values per column go into the tool's context — GA-18's lesson that values teach better than names. The semantic layer rides along as a config file — 'revenue = amount where status = SHIPPED' — versioned, injected with the schema. Session semantics: each conversation gets its own in-process DuckDB connection — user A's uploaded data is structurally unreachable from user B's queries, the per-session isolation doing what GA-17's ACL filters do at retrieval.

scenes.title: Ingestion with honesty about every rejected row
scenes.body:
import duckdb

def ingest(csv_path: str, session: str) -> IngestReport:
    con = sessions.connect(session)             # per-user isolation
    con.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE staging AS
        SELECT * FROM read_csv(?, all_varchar=True)
    """, [csv_path])

    # type inference with explicit rejects
    con.execute("""
        CREATE VIEW orders AS
        SELECT
          TRY_CAST(order_id AS BIGINT) AS order_id,
          TRY_CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS amount,
          TRY_CAST(order_date AS DATE) AS order_date
        FROM staging
        WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL AND amount IS NOT NULL
    """)
    rejected = con.execute("""
        SELECT * FROM staging
        WHERE order_id IS NULL OR amount IS NULL
    """).fetchall()

    return IngestReport(
        rows_loaded=con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders").fetchone()[0],
        rows_rejected=len(rejected),
        reject_sample=rejected[:5],          # shown to user, not hidden
        schema=con.execute("DESCRIBE orders").fetchall(),
    )
annot: TRY_CAST + explicit reject count: bad rows are REPORTED, not silently coerced to NULL and dropped from awareness
reject_sample in the report: the user sees WHAT failed and can fix the source
Per-session connections: the isolation is structural — user B's tables don't exist in user A's catalog
scenes.narration: The report object is a design choice with consequences: the agent's first message after ingest states coverage honestly — 'loaded 48,206 rows, rejected 14 — 9 had unparsable dates, 5 negative amounts' — GA-19's 'state coverage explicitly' rule, implemented as data. Rejections with samples turn 'the numbers look off' conversations into 'fix these 14 rows' actions. The view layer earns its keep when the model writes SQL: it queries 'orders', not 'staging' or file paths — a namespace you control, where the types are already right, where you can add the semantic-layer columns — 'revenue' as a computed view — so the model asks the BUSINESS question, not the column-guessing question. And the per-session connection is the tenant boundary: no cross-user where-clauses needed because the tables themselves don't coexist — the strongest isolation is structural.

scenes.title: The DuckDB SQL tool: **fenced like GA-18, described like AG-02**
scenes.narration: The agent's primary tool is run-sql — the GA-18 safety gate, DuckDB edition. Description, AG-02 style: 'Execute read-only SQL over the current session's tables. Use for aggregation, filtering, joins, and trend questions. Do NOT use for file writes, ATTACH, or COPY — those are rejected. Prefer explicit column lists over SELECT *.' The fences, all four: PARSE — sqlglot parses the query, rejecting anything that isn't a clean SELECT; ALLOW-LIST — AST walk rejects ATTACH, COPY, file functions, anything touching the filesystem; WRAP — every query gets LIMIT 500 injected, bounding results regardless of what the model wrote; and IDENTITY — the DuckDB connection runs with no access beyond its session views, so even a clever jailbreak finds no database credentials to abuse. Errors return as observations — 'column status does not exist — available columns: order_id, amount, order_date' — GA-18's actionable-error discipline, closing the self-correction loop.

items.s: Parse → AST allow-list → LIMIT wrap → session-scoped identity · defense even against jailbroken models
Unknown columns name the available ones · syntax errors quote the position · the loop self-corrects
'sum/compare/count' → SQL · 'show/plot' → code route · 'what does it say' → retrieval route (GA-19)

scenes.narration: The tool description's 'prefer explicit column lists' hint is small and load-bearing: it steers the model away from SELECT-star habits that waste context on irrelevant columns — description discipline shaping behavior, AG-02's lesson at tool scale. The router — GA-19's triage — lives in the agent's instructions: three question classes, three engines, and the model learns quickly which phrasing goes where; verify with a golden set — twenty questions per route, misroutes measured, instructions tuned until routing accuracy holds. One more tool belongs in the set: list-tables — the model's map, answering 'what data exists here' before it queries — the exploration-before-action pattern from AG-03. With ingest plus two tools, the agent already answers most analytical questions correctly; charts complete the experience.

scenes.title: Charts and summaries: **the code route, sandboxed**
scenes.sub: matplotlib in the sandbox, artifacts out
scenes.narration: When the question wants a picture — 'plot monthly revenue' — the agent writes Python: pandas over the DuckDB results, matplotlib for the chart; a sandbox executes it — AG-03's contract: no network, resource caps, ephemeral workspace; the chart returns as an artifact — stored, linked, viewable — with the agent's narrative alongside: 'Revenue climbed through Q2, dipped in July — the dip tracks the pricing change in your notes.' Summaries follow the same discipline: the numbers come from SQL — the engine computes; the WORDS come from the model — it interprets, it cannot alter. The composition rule from GA-19 is the integrity invariant: the agent may never state a number that didn't pass through the SQL tool — if it quotes a figure, the trace shows the query that produced it — citations for arithmetic, the same grounded-answer discipline as GA-16, one layer down.

layers.s: analysis → SQL tool · visual → sandbox code · semantic → retrieval
DuckDB exact · sandbox matplotlib · artifacts linked
Narrative cites every number · 'July revenue: 214k (query #7)' · speculation labeled as such

scenes.narration: The interpretive layer has honesty rules worth writing into the system prompt: cite or hedge — every quantitative claim carries its query reference, every inference carries language like 'suggests' or 'correlates with'; state coverage — when the answer rests on sampled or filtered data, say so — 'based on 48k shipped orders, excluding the 14 rejected rows'; and abstain on under-determination — 'the data can't tell us WHY July dipped — it shows WHAT happened; possible explanations need information I don't have' — GA-16's abstention discipline, adapted. These aren't politeness; they're what separates an analyst agent from a plausible-numbers machine, and they're evaluable — the golden set includes 'unanswerable why' cases where the correct response names the gap. The chart route inherits the same rules: axes labeled, units stated, source query referenced in the caption.

scenes.title: Guardrails, evals, and the honesty budget
scenes.sub: What makes THIS analyst trustworthy enough to ship
scenes.narration: Close the project with its production story. GUARDRAILS: input length caps on uploads; the SQL fences from chapter one; output screens — the narrative passes a PII and secret check before display — GA-23's gates, nothing novel, everything present. EVALS: a golden analyst set — forty questions with known answers over a fixture dataset, including traps — 'total revenue including refunds' where the semantic layer says refunds are excluded, 'average by month' with a month missing from the data — measuring not just correctness but HONESTY: does the agent note the missing month? AG-18's trajectory metrics apply to the SQL: is the query sensible, or does it flail? COST: per-task metering — AG-18's efficiency gates — an analytical question should cost cents; regression-test it. And the limits, stated in the product itself: 'I answer from the data you've given me; I can't tell you why without more information; I'll always show my queries if you ask' — the user's mental model, set honestly, is the final guardrail.

items.s: 40+ questions, known answers, traps (refunds, missing months) · correctness AND honesty scored
Cents per question, queries per task · AG-18's efficiency regressions block promotion
"I answer from your data, I show my work, I say when I can't" · the user's honest mental model

scenes.narration: The build order, like the last project: one — ingest with reject-reporting, tested on messy CSVs; two — the fenced SQL tool, Inspector-tested, jailbreak-probed ('write a query that drops the table' should hit the AST fence); three — routing golden set until triage accuracy holds; four — the sandbox chart route with artifact plumbing; five — the narrative honesty rules, eval-tested on trap questions. What this project proves at completion: GA-19's routing architecture, GA-18's fenced SQL, AG-03's sandboxing, and GA-16's grounded-answer discipline compose into ONE coherent product — an analyst that computes exactly, interprets honestly, shows its work, and costs pennies a question. Two projects remain in the stage: documents and messaging — the same disciplines, new shapes.

recap: Ingest CSV→Parquet with explicit reject reporting and per-session isolation; views give the model a typed, semantic-layered namespace
The SQL tool carries GA-18's four fences and AG-02's actionable errors; routing sends analysis to SQL, visuals to the sandbox, semantics to retrieval
Narrative cites every number via query references and abstains on whys; golden sets score honesty; efficiency gates keep questions at cents

quiz.q: Why report rejected rows with samples instead of silently coercing them?
opts: Silent data loss corrupts every downstream answer — visible rejects turn 'numbers look off' into fixable source-data actions
quiz.why: Coverage honesty is analytical correctness: an agent that hides 14 rejected rows answers confidently on a dataset the user thinks is complete.

quiz.q: What's the integrity invariant for the agent's narrative?
opts: Every stated number passed through the SQL tool and carries a query reference — the model interprets but cannot alter
quiz.why: Citations for arithmetic: separating computation (engine) from interpretation (model) is the project's core trust architecture.

quiz.q: Why include 'unanswerable why' cases in the golden set?
opts: Honesty under under-determination is the differentiating skill — a correct 'the data can't tell us why' beats a confident invented reason
quiz.why: Analyst agents fail most dangerously by confabulating causes; the eval measures the abstention discipline that prevents it (GA-16/AG-18).

code.title: run-sql: the whole tool
code.body:
@mcp.tool()
def run_sql(query: str, session: str) -> SqlResult:
    """Execute read-only SQL over this session's tables (orders, …).
    Use for aggregation, joins, trends. Do NOT use for file ops —
    ATTACH/COPY/read_csv are rejected. Prefer explicit column lists.
    Results capped at 500 rows."""
    tree = sqlglot.parse_one(query)
    if not isinstance(tree, sqlglot.exp.Select) or \
       any(banned in tree.sql() for banned in
           ("ATTACH", "COPY", "read_csv", "write_")):
        raise ToolError("only plain SELECTs over session tables allowed")
    con = sessions.connect(session)          # structural isolation
    rows = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM ({tree.sql()}) _q LIMIT 500")
    return SqlResult(columns=rows.columns, rows=rows.fetchall(),
                     row_count=rows.rowcount, query=tree.sql())
annot: session is server-side state, never a tool argument the model controls — structural isolation, not prompt pleading
The result carries its own query: narrative citations are free
row_count teaches the model when a LIMIT clipped the answer — 'showing 500 of N' honesty
